result.title: Spec$^2$R: Recovering Emergent Properties in Supervised Vision Transformers
result.summary: Vision Transformers (ViTs) have achieved strong performance across computer vision tasks, but the quality of their learned representations differs drastically depending on the training paradigm. While self-supervised ViTs often demonstrate emergent properties, such as object-aligned patch representations and attention maps, supervised ViTs typically lack these properties, even when trained with strong data augmentations. Understanding the origin of this difference is important for explaining and controlling the object-level structure. To investigate it, we perform a spectral analysis of supervised and self-supervised models, and identify a key distinction: MLP layers in supervised ViTs introduce high-frequency variations into patch representations, disrupting their spatial organization. Motivated by this finding, we propose Spec$^2$R, a lightweight spectral regularization method that fine-tunes the MLP layers of pretrained supervised ViTs. Spec$^2$R recovers object-aligned patch representations and attention maps, while improving adversarial robustness and preserving competitive classification accuracy.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文对监督式与自监督 ViT 做频谱分析，发现监督 ViT 的 MLP 层向 patch 表示引入高频扰动、破坏其空间组织，并提出轻量频谱正则 Spec²R 微调 MLP 层，以恢复物体对齐的 patch 表示与注意力图，同时提升对抗鲁棒性并保持分类精度。
